A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe Digital Twin Catalog and include matching main sections, references, and Appendices A–C. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to pages 1 and 3.

before.justification: V1 reports original inverse-rendering and egocentric reconstruction benchmarks, simulated robotic manipulation results, and supplementary sparse-view reconstruction experiments (Tables 2–4 and 6–8).

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark, reconstruction, and robotic manipulation results, including the experiments in Appendix B and details in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The dataset acquisition and alignment procedures, LRM-VolSDF architecture in Appendix B, and robotic policy architectures and objectives in Appendix C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DTC DSLR and active/passive egocentric data, GSO evaluation, and robotic pushing and grasping tasks involving DTC, Objaverse-XL, and the Stanford-ORB test cup. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The six inverse-rendering baselines, 3D-GS/2D-GS, MeshLRM comparison, and Objaverse-XL robotics comparison are unchanged. Correcting 'Stanford Orb' to 'Stanford-ORB' in Table 1 does not introduce a different comparator.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendices A–C retain identical splits, view-selection procedures, image preprocessing, metrics, training settings, and testing protocols, including the sparse-view and robotics experiments.

E4.justification: The geometric and material case comparisons, sparse-view reconstruction analyses, egocentric reconstruction comparisons, and pushing-success threshold analysis are retained unchanged (Appendix B and Figure 8).

E5.justification: Table 4 still reports sample standard deviations over three policy-training seeds, and Figure 8 retains the corresponding uncertainty shading. Statistical reporting elsewhere, including dataset statistics in Table 5, is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–8 and the qualitative results retain identical values, rankings, and examples. For instance, DTC-trained pushing success at the 2 cm threshold remains 36.3% ± 1.5% in Table 4.

T1.justification: The policy definitions, action-sampling formulas, and mathematical descriptions are unchanged. Neither version contains a theorem or proof contribution that is added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a 2,000-object photorealistic digital-twin dataset, DSLR and egocentric evaluation benchmarks, and benefits for robotic manipulation. The abstract copyedits preserve these claims and their scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reconstruction quality, synthetic-to-real domain gaps, and robotics performance are identical. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning acquisition effort, object size, deformability, specularity, transparency, and simulation-to-real transfer.

D1.justification: Acquisition details, preprocessing instructions, architectures, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain identical, including Appendix C. Dataset access information and the promised future release of baseline evaluations are unchanged; hyperlink targets also match.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Table 1 corrects the spelling of Stanford-ORB while retaining reference [39], the same dataset attributes, and the existing comparison.

P1.justification: V2 adds 'the' before Digital Twin Catalog in the abstract, adjusts hyphenation and punctuation, corrects 'Stanford Orb' to 'Stanford-ORB' in Table 1, and updates the arXiv version/date header. Section organization and appendix prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract has localized line reflow, and Table 1 displays the corrected dataset label. Figures, table structures, captions, and placements are otherwise unchanged; all pages except 1 and 3 render identically.

improvement.justification: V2 provides small editorial polish through abstract copyedits and consistent Stanford-ORB naming. The scientific content, experimental evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—remain unchanged, so these localized corrections do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
